free_tier.stated: NVMe - X at USD 5.00/month: 1 CPU core, 2048 MB RAM, 30 GB NVMe, 2000 GB/month bandwidth, 100 Mbps, IPv4 plus IPv6. The billing portal's Tokyo store lists it as 'Tokyo Linux NVMe Cloud X Starting from $5.00 USD Monthly Order Now' - monthly term, in stock; annual and renewal prices are not published, and the portal's product detail pages redirect to a fallback category, so no per-cycle price is reachable. The plan table publishes one order button per location: London, Amsterdam, Barcelona, Moscow, Johannesburg, Mumbai, Singapore, Sydney, Taiwan, Tokyo, Seoul, Los Angeles, Dallas, Chicago, Ashburn, Sao Paulo. The next step up, NVMe - 1, is USD 10.00 with 1 core, 4096 MB and 60 GB at 250 Mbps.

egress.terms: bandwidth is stated per plan and per location: 2000 GB a month on the X plan in most locations, 100 GB on the Taiwan row as listed by the tracker; no overage price was published on the page read
egress.free_allowance: 2000 GB/month on the X plan; 100 GB/month on Taiwan per the tracker

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: WHMCS billing portal at photonvps.com/billing with a client area, registration and knowledgebase; no API was stated on the pages read
record.chaining: USD 5.00 for 2 GB and 30 GB of NVMe in Tokyo, Seoul or Singapore is the cheapest APAC capacity among documented hosts and the only one with a 2 GB entry plan. The 100 Mbps port and the 2 TB cap make it a crawler worker rather than a serving host, and it is this category's best option for a source that only answers from an Asian IP.

limits.value: 2000 GB a month on the X plan at 100 Mbps. The allowance is per location and not uniform: the tracker's Taiwan row for the same X plan states 100 GB/month, twenty times smaller, so a Taiwan box would exhaust its allowance in about three days of continuous 100 Mbps traffic by arithmetic.
